description: This donut chart, a variation of a pie chart, illustrates the distribution of various categories under the heading "Stimulus Type," which is printed in bold black text in the center hole. The chart is divided into 10 distinct slices. Moving clockwise from the top right, the categories and their specified proportions are: a red slice for "Draft/Other" (26.4%), a dark brown slice for "Event Posting" (6.6%), a mauve slice for "Organizational Report" (7.7%), another similarly colored mauve slice for "Organizational Website" (4.9%), a dark blue slice for "Interview" (8.8%), a light blue slice for "Intra-agency news article" (4.9%), a dark green slice for "External News Article" (18.1%), a light green slice for "Email" (2.7%), a yellow-gold slice for "Press Release" (18.7%), and a thin orange slice for "Social Media Post" (1.1%). The chart does not use a separate legend; instead, all category labels and their corresponding percentages in parentheses are positioned outside the ring, adjacent to their respective segments. The segments are not arranged in any specific order, such as descending or ascending size, and no individual slices are visually emphasized through explosion or offset.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of various input stimulus material types provided by journalists to LLMs during WildChat conversations, matched to online articles from two identified news agencies. The largest category is 'Draft/Other,' accounting for approximately 26.4% of the total, followed by 'Press Release' at 18.7%. 'External News Article' and 'Interview' are the next largest categories, representing 18.1% and 8.8%, respectively. Notably, 'Organizational Report' consistently exceeds 'Event Posting,' with 9.7% compared to 6.6%. Additionally, 'Social Media Post' shows a slight increase over 'Email,' with 1.5% versus 2.7%. The chart provides a clear overview of the relative proportions of each stimulus type, with all categories labeled and color-coded for clarity.
